findings.evidence: Lines 39-42: the proof is `intro i; exact MemLp.of_bound (hf.comp_aemeasurable (hX i)).aestronglyMeasurable C (ae_of_all μ fun ω => hf_bound (X i ω))` — `i` appears only as an argument selector. `MemLp.of_bound` is Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/LpSeminorm/Basic.lean:549 and takes a single function.
findings.fix: Export the index-free lemma, e.g. `theorem memLp_comp_of_bound {g : Ω → α} (hf : Measurable f) (hg : AEMeasurable g μ) (C : ℝ) (hf_bound : ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ C) (p : ENNReal) : MemLp (fun ω => f (g ω)) p μ`, and define `memLp_comp_process_of_bound := fun i => memLp_comp_of_bound hf (hX i) C hf_bound p` if the family form is still wanted for feeding `contractable_covariance_structure`.
findings.issue: The statement's mathematical content is entirely per-coordinate — `MemLp (f ∘ g) p μ` from `Measurable f`, `AEMeasurable g`, `∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ C` — but the public form quantifies over a ℕ-indexed process `X : ℕ → Ω → α` and returns `∀ i`. The index is free data the proof never uses (the body is `intro i; exact MemLp.of_bound ...`). A consumer holding a single measurable `g : Ω → α` and a bounded `f` cannot apply this lemma without instantiating `X := fun _ => g` and then projecting at an arbitrary index; nothing in the name or signature signals that this generic Lᵖ fact is index-independent.

summary: The exported `memLp_comp_process_of_bound` bakes a ℕ-indexed family into what is a single-function fact, so no consumer can use it for one observable without inventing a dummy process. Split off the index-free lemma and derive the family version from it.
